ops.title: slop-cop's LLM tiers are non-deterministic; never gate CI on them
ops.body:
## Fact, measured 2026-07-31

`slop-cop check --llm-effort=high` returns a different violation set on repeated runs against **identical, unedited bytes**.

`skills/slop-cop-prose/SKILL.md`, three consecutive runs, no edits between them:

    run 1 → 0 violations
    run 2 → 1 violation  (term-consistency)
    run 3 → 0 violations

`README.md` across three editing rounds: the count fell 6 → 3 → 3, but the *identity* of every violation changed each round.

    round 1: triple-construction x3, term-consistency x2, one-point-dilution
    round 2: one-point-dilution, term-consistency, triple-construction
    round 3: one-point-dilution, term-consistency, unnecessary-elaboration

Each editing pass rewrote prose the next pass did not flag, while the model found new spans in prose it had previously passed.

## Consequences

- **Do not gate CI on an LLM-effort run.** The build would flake. Gate on `--llm-effort=off`, which is deterministic, or on `--standard=slop --llm-effort=off` for the pre-base-layer contract.
- **Do not chase LLM-tier zero on a document.** It is not a property of the prose; it is a sample. Past roughly two rounds, further editing degrades good writing to satisfy noise.
- Concretely, chasing it cost the README real content before this was understood: "pre-commit" was dropped from the tagline, "JSX" from a section heading (contradicting the paragraph directly beneath it), "polish" from the skill description, and "no highlighting" from the agent-interface claim — each cut to defuse a `triple-construction` flag that did not reappear on a later run. All were reverted.

## What the LLM tiers are good for

Advisory review of a draft, where a human or agent judges each hit. They are not a gate, and `counts_by_rule == {}` at high effort is not a reproducible state.

The `slop-cop-prose` skill already documents a stylistic-choice escape hatch and now caps its loop at 4 passes for this reason.
